- Archives reject unsafe/duplicate paths: - Archives reject unsafe/duplicate paths, symlinks, encrypted ZIP entries, invalid directories, multi-volume/ZIP64 directories and unsupported concatenated compressed streams. ZIP expansion ratios are bounded. TAR decompression is bounded before member/PAX parsing, with an additional fixed 4 MiB allowance for TAR headers/padding; XZ decoder memory is limited too.
- Decryption accepts only the OneKit enc: - Decryption accepts only the OneKit encrypted format and authenticates its contents before bounded archive restoration. User options cannot increase the enforced expansion budget.
- Fonts require matching SFNT/WOFF heade: - Fonts require matching SFNT/WOFF headers, valid bounded table ranges and coherent compressed-font sizes. Declared WOFF expansion cannot exceed the font byte budget.
- Inspection, metadata adapters and encr: - Inspection, metadata adapters and encryption intentionally accept arbitrary file types. Their count/byte limits still apply. Inspecting a damaged or unknown file is a supported operation, rather than a reason to reject it solely for its content.

- PDF tools require PDF headers and a co: - PDF tools require PDF headers and a coherent final cross-reference location. `pdf-repair` deliberately permits damaged cross-references after checking the PDF header; its parser still has to recover an actual PDF. Images renamed to `.pdf` are rejected.

- Word, Excel and PowerPoint require dis: - Word, Excel and PowerPoint require distinct ZIP container parts and namespaced XML roots. Renaming Excel to `.docx` does not turn it into Word. - `image-remove-watermark`: requires `re: - `image-remove-watermark`: requires `regions`; uses the same local reconstruction. It estimates missing pixels and cannot recover hidden original content. Texture, large marks and intricate backgrounds may give poor results.
- `image-repair`: without `regions`, app: - `image-repair`: without `regions`, applies a median filter of `size` 3 or 5 to isolated speckles. With regions, reconstructs selected pixels using fixed surrounding pixels and discrete harmonic diffusion (`iterations` 10–500, default 200).
- `image-sharpen`: `method` is `unsharp`: - `image-sharpen`: `method` is `unsharp` (default) or `deconvolution`. `radius` 0.3–5 sets the unsharp radius or estimated Gaussian point spread. Unsharp `amount` 0–300 percent (default 150). Richardson–Lucy uses 1–30 `iterations` (default 10), reflect padding and FFT convolution, up to one million source pixels. It assumes Gaussian blur and does not correct arbitrary motion. Both may amplify noise and halos.
- `jpg-to-svg`: `colors` (2–32, default: - `jpg-to-svg`: `colors` (2–32, default 16), `resolution` (32–512, default 256). Quantizes a bounded image, merges horizontal equal-color runs vertically, and writes filled SVG paths. No bitmap is embedded. This produces vector tiles with a posterized appearance, not smooth curve tracing.
- `pdf-make-fillable`: `fields` is a JSO: - `pdf-make-fillable`: `fields` is a JSON array of standard AcroForm widgets with unique ASCII `name`, `type` (`text`, `checkbox`, `choice`), 1-based `page`, normalized `x`, `y`, `width`, `height`. Optional `required`, text `multiline`, and choice `choices` are supported. Existing fields and page content are preserved. Duplicate names, encrypted PDFs and XFA are rejected. No automatic blank recognition.
- `pdf-remove-watermark`: default `mode:: - `pdf-remove-watermark`: default `mode: "remove"` removes `/Artifact` groups tagged `/Subtype /Watermark` (including named property resources) and `/Watermark` annotations. Optional `text` matches full text objects with whitespace normalized, decoding glyphs through their font encoding/ToUnicode map. Nested Form XObjects are processed recursively. Use `mode: "inspect"` to get a JSON report of text, image and form invocation IDs; pass selected IDs as `objects` in remove mode. Selecting a form removes its entire graphic group. Modified forms are copied per invocation so unselected uses of a shared resource remain unchanged. IDs refer to the same original PDF and must be reinspected after changes. This is drawing-object removal, not secure redaction: unused resource objects may remain in the output. It does not identify arbitrary untagged content as a watermark automatically, and a mark merged into a scanned image cannot be separated from that image. A report contains up to 2,000 candidates, recursion is limited to 12 levels and processing to 300,000 drawing operations. Zero matches produces an explicit error.
